description:
The Keplerian transfer arc rendered on /fly has the correct endpoints (Earth at departure, destination at arrival) but the middle of the arc bulges on the wrong side of the chord — the retrograde/mirror ellipse is selected instead of the prograde half-ellipse, producing a visually incorrect bulge. The bug is invisible to the current test suite because neither mission-arc.test.ts nor trajectory-soundness.test.ts test arc direction.

Expected: The outbound transfer arc should be the short prograde (CCW) half-ellipse from p1 to p2: the midpoint of the arc must be on the CCW side of the chord (p2−p1). The arc endpoints must keep their exact input positions.

Acceptance criteria:
- The arc midpoint (index = steps/2) must be on the CCW side of the chord: compute cross product chordX = p2.x−p1.x, chordZ = p2.z−p1.z, midX = arc[midIdx].x, midZ = arc[midIdx].z, midOffsetX = midX − (p1.x+p2.x)/2, midOffsetZ = midZ − (p1.z+p2.z)/2. The cross product (chordX * midOffsetZ − chordZ * midOffsetX) must be > 0 for every pair of distinct input positions (p1, p2) passed to transferEllipse. [spec: src/lib/mission-arc.ts lines 135-140: 'sweeping from p1 to p2 in the CCW (prograde) direction' and 'Direction: prograde (CCW) sweep from p1's heliocentric angle to p2's heliocentric angle.']
- Both endpoints must match p1 and p2 exactly (within 1e-8 floating-point tolerance). Existing trajectory-soundness tests verify this for 36 missions; they must continue to pass after a fix. [code-invariant: transferEllipse constructs an ellipse through both input positions. The arc is not a valid solution if endpoints drift.]
- No regression in the existing 325+ trajectory-soundness tests (trajectory-soundness.test.ts: finiteness, endpoint proximity, length, spacecraftPos continuity, V∞ shaping bounds). The fix must not introduce NaN, infinite values, or endpoint drift for any of the 36 missions. [code-invariant: trajectory-soundness.test.ts — the full test battery is the regression oracle.]

Domain facts:
- The two F2 candidates produce mirror-image ellipses; one produces the CCW prograde half-ellipse, the other produces the retrograde/CW mirror. The correct F2 is the one on the CCW side of the chord: perpendicular vector perp = (-dz/chord, +dx/chord) points to the CCW side, so the correct F2 is F2candidates[0] (mx + h*perpX, mz + h*perpZ) — the +perp variant. The current heuristic compares nu_sweep (ellipse parameter space, always in [0, 2π)) against desiredSweep (heliocentric angle gap, also in [0, 2π)), which are different geometric quantities and do not correlate.
- The /plan page allows choosing Mercury and Venus as destinations (9 destinations total). Any user-created plan to Mercury or Venus, or any future Mercury/Venus library mission, would hit this bug when the destination is 'behind' Earth in CCW terms (desiredSweep > π).
- The existing 36 library missions are all Mars (16), Moon (16), or outer planets (4: Jupiter, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres). For all of these, desiredSweep < π, so the current heuristic accidentally selects the correct F2. The bug is a latent failure waiting for inner-planet geometry.

Target: src/lib/mission-arc.ts — transferEllipse
Do NOT change The current F2 selection heuristic (lines 176-192) compares nu_sweep against desiredSweep — these are different geometric quantities (ellipse parameter space vs heliocentric angle) and do not correlate. The heuristic is not salvageable; the correct F2 is the +perp variant (F2candidates[0]: mx + h*perpX, mz + h*perpZ) which lies on the CCW side of the chord. Do not re-derive a heuristic from desiredSweep. — it is not the owner of this symptom.
